title: Partition into K Equal-Sum Groups
statement: A warehouse must load a set of crates onto exactly k trucks. You are given a list of positive integers nums, where nums[i] is the weight of crate i, and an integer k >= 1. Every crate must be loaded onto exactly one truck, every truck must carry at least one crate, and all k trucks must end up carrying exactly the same total weight. Write can_split_shipments(nums, k) that returns True if such a loading exists and False otherwise. Return the single boolean only. Obvious rejections apply: if the total weight is not divisible by k, or any single crate weighs more than total/k, the answer is False. Inputs have at most ~12 crates, so an exhaustive search with pruning must finish.
hints: Greedily dropping each crate into the first truck it fits on can dead-end even when a valid loading exists — what technique lets you undo a placement and try a different truck?

Keep an array of k running bucket sums; recursively assign crates one at a time (largest first), only into buckets that stay <= total/k, and subtract the weight back out when a recursive call fails. Skip buckets whose current sum equals one you already tried for this crate, and stop after trying an empty bucket (symmetry pruning).

Compute target = sum(nums)//k after checking divisibility and max(nums) <= target. Sort descending. place(i): if i == len(nums) return True; for each bucket with an unseen sum, if buckets[b] + nums[i] <= target then add, recurse on i+1, and on failure subtract it back; break after an empty bucket. Return place(0).
